title: fix_tmp_space.sh: 30G /tmp tmpfs, live user cap, 64G /var/disktmp
objective: Commands stop failing with EDQUOT on /tmp: the tmpfs grows to 30G without an unmount, each logged-in user's cap rises live to 80% of it, and a 64G disk-backed temp area exists at /var/disktmp for heavy writers to use later through TMPDIR.
acceptance_criteria: `sudo fix_tmp_space.sh` on a stock machine writes the tmp.mount drop-in, the fstab line and the tmpfiles entry, reloads systemd once, remounts /tmp at size=30G and keeps usrquota, files and X11 sockets in /tmp.
Each non-root uid under /run/user gets a cap of 80% of 30G live (25165824 KiB); a cap of 0 or one already within 1 MiB is left alone.
/var/disktmp is a mounted 64G sparse ext4 image, mode 1777; a file written there by a user lands in the image.
A second run changes nothing and prints one line; --verify-only changes nothing, works without root and exits non-zero on drift.
After a reboot /tmp is 30G from the drop-in, systemd applies its own 80% cap at login, and /var/disktmp is mounted and emptied by tmpfiles.
out_of_scope: Pointing heavy writers at /var/disktmp through TMPDIR.
Running the script on the host (the coordinator does that after review).
verifier: test_tmp_space_apply.sh (42 passed), test_tmp_space_verify.sh (36 passed), test_tmp_quota.py (11 passed); every phase of vmbox_tmp_space.sh OK in guest tmpspace, including the reboot and a fail-open boot without the image.
